build: Svelte 5 + Vite + Tailwind, static-first. Tracks the applicant field (280+ applicants researched across seven platforms) and renders it as a live, filterable showcase.
name: Ice Cream Market Monitor
pitch: A global ice-cream market monitor built as the portfolio piece for the Snoop Dogg x Deel application.
problem: A hiring campaign this big deserves more than a resume — it deserves proof of shipping. The monitor answers 'what does DOGS actually build?' with live data, not slides.
result: Live at icecream.wearedogs.net. Became the flagship demo of the ecosystem and the supporting material for the application.

build: Svelte + Tauri config GUI writes an OS-agnostic config file; a Ventoy-style boot menu (WinPE + Linux rescue) reads it headlessly. PowerShell for Windows-side scripts, bash twins for Linux-side. Serious safety interlocks on the nuke path.
name: Phoenix
pitch: One USB stick, any PC on Earth, back to your personalized Windows — backup, nuke, reinstall in one flow.
problem: Rebuilding a Windows machine from scratch is a day of clicking through installers. Phoenix turns it into: plug in, walk away, done.
result: In active development — the top priority workstream in the org.

build: QEMU/WHPX virtualization on a home server, VPN tunneling, DNS filtering. A router replacement with built-in local network storage is the north-star hardware vision.
name: Project Castle
pitch: The home server and private cloud: VMs, network storage, VPN, DNS filtering — the family data vault.
problem: Family data scattered across rented clouds is a liability. Castle brings it home: local-first storage with encrypted offsite backup.
result: Running as the org's backup target and private cloud. Family-data-vault and true-deletion ('flamethrower') specs are in the repo docs.

build: Discogs new-release/stock/resale tracking with drop alerts over email and SMS. Alert-engine plan is specced in the repo docs.
name: Wax
pitch: Vinyl drop alerts and resale tracking — Discogs-powered monitoring with a $10/mo subscription lane.
problem: Rare pressings sell out in minutes and resell at 5x. Collectors need to know the second a drop or restock happens.
result: Second money lane for the org after the divorce checkout. Alert engine in build.

build: Step-by-step flow generating a printable divorce packet. The money milestone: a real $30 test payment on staging that produces the packet.
name: Divorce
pitch: Fixed-price DIY divorce flow that ends in a printable packet — checkout first, then everything else.
problem: DIY divorce paperwork is a maze of forms and filing rules. A guided flow with a real checkout turns a legal headache into a product.
result: Public repo, staging on GitHub Pages. Twenty skeletons don't make money — one checkout page does.

build: Extracted from Castle's saves into a standalone tool. Save-versioning with cloud sync, shaped for SNES/GBA-era emulators.
name: Chains
pitch: "Git for save data" — version control for retro game saves, emulator-compatible, with cloud sync.
problem: One lost save file, hours of progress gone. Born from exactly that.
result: Private repo in the org, in active build.

build: Stdlib-only Python CLI: a recipe TOML describes the swarm, shell/fixture backends spawn agents, and the docs spec a sandboxed-agent threat model.
name: Bakery
pitch: Multi-AI orchestration: one command fans work to Kite, Claude, and Gemini, then merges their reports automatically.
problem: Hand-carrying reports between AIs is slow and lossy. Bakery spawns a swarm of parallel agents, tracks them, and merges the results into one document.
result: Working `bake report` end-to-end on a fixture example; the multi-AI endgame is specced in VISION.md.

build: Native Kotlin Android app. Magic Mode probes IR codes (Samsung first); Manual Mode is a full remote pad with rate-limited blast mode; attempt log records every probe.
name: DOGS Remote
pitch: A native Android app that turns a phone with an IR blaster into a universal TV remote.
problem: Hotel bars and venues: the TV needs changing and nobody has the remote. Magic Mode finds the working IR code in seconds, IT WORKED saves the venue profile.
result: Private org repo, built for the OnePlus 12R IR blaster; APK building.

build: A Python builder fetches public repo metadata into data.json under a safe-fields allowlist (PII blocklist aborts the build); static page served from gh-pages.
name: DOGS Mission Control
pitch: The public, zero-PII status board for the YEAHDOGS org — every repo's health at a glance.
problem: ~20 skeletons and counting need a single pulse check. The dashboard shows per-repo health (commits, issues, Actions status, Pages links) with no personal data collected.
result: Live on GitHub Pages; refreshed hourly by the octopus loop.
